Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:

reaching the cap is charged the full cap. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until

# Continual-ARC

1. Parse the grid, caps, and action schema. Treat each instance as independent and use only its demonstrations. Infer output dimensions and a full mapping for roles, boundaries, direction, extent, and collisions; verify the rule against every pair before applying it. For periodic/diagonal patterns, derive an explicit coordinate rule (modulus, orientation, phase) and verify successive rows and columns. Never infer a stripe, translation, reflection, or fill rule from resemblance alone.
3. For line-completion puzzles, verify the exact completion geometry from demos: determine whether gaps are filled only between collinear endpoints, whether endpoints can be in separate segments, and whether existing markers interrupt or bound lines. Do not extrapolate every row/column between global extrema unless the demo establishes that.

After receiving it, explicitly eliminate or retain the alternatives. Avoid additional demos when the examples already establish a consistent rule or no specific distinction remains.

Do not repeat or tweak a failed candidate without evidence distinguishing the new rule. If still underdetermined, request a targeted demo while its expected value justifies the cost; do not burn submissions on near-identical guesses.
